column1: # D6's pass conditions for HR-25's fix (brief P4-4-HR25, deliverable 2), written before any counted run and before any build of Option A.
# This file decides, with resync-cases.tsv. Why each row is here: docs/phase4/D6-hr25-resync-conditions.md.
# op and value are a row's threshold or pinned value, where it has one. Any edit changes this file's SHA-256: test_resync_conditions.py pins it.

column5: rule
C0: Zeek as on main, the zeek/zeek image at pins.env's ZEEK_IMAGE, with today's script (HR-23 note 4.1). A control.
C1p: the project's build from option (i)'s pinned inputs without a patch, with the script with part (a) (HR-23 note 4.1). A control.
C2: the option (i) build, with the script with part (a) (HR-23 note 4.1). A control, and the baseline that A is judged against.

C2A: the (i)+A image named by digest, the image that ships (design 4, C2), with the shipped script: the script with part (a) and A's script part (the eight new weird names and the existing dnp3_ ones in Weird::sampling_global_list, the resync rows, resync_cause, the per-end mark field). Its values are this file's val- rows. A run of a rebuild is not this configuration.
The four configurations run in one run, on the same captures, on the same runner image. A result from another run is not carried over.

F, per connection, before confirmation (design 2.7). Above the benign maximum of 5: a TCP sensor start costs 4 (dnp3-resync-tcp-r2-midstream-both), and a link-layer retry of the first frame 1 more (dnp3-resync-udp-link-retry-first). Reachable by the fuzz harness: 8 failures fit in 64 chunks.

O, per connection, before confirmation. Above the benign maximum of 582 octets: a TCP sensor start that lands inside a frame on each end scans at most 291 octets per end. Reachable within fuzz-max-len.
K, resync rows per interval across the host. The overflow row is not counted against K (design 2.8, D6's B6).
Seconds.

Zeek's value (init-bare.zeek at v9.0.1), which the shipped script keeps until D2 answers S9. If the shipped script redefines it, the five fragment-limit cases are rebuilt from the new value by the same rules, in a new commit of both files before the run.

Only if S5's ratio is exceeded and the bound is added (design 2.10). Its four cases are the route bound rows of resync-cases.tsv; they are judged only if the bound is added, and are not run otherwise.

For each S5 input, its CPU time is at most 5 times that of valid DNP3 of the same octets and transport (s5- rows). Above it on any input, the bound of val-R is added before the image is fixed, A's patch is pinned again, and the counted run measures the rebuilt image.

Labels come from how each case was built (T1). The builder records every frame as valid or as the failure it carries, and every message as seen, absent or lost. tshark's reading is reported beside them, and a difference is reported, never used as a label.

Rule 6 of D6-engine-run-pass-conditions.md section 1 does not hold for dnp3-resync-*: a function row on a case's flows that the labels lack fails the case under C2A. Rule 9 holds, with the count exact: n labelled rows of a (flow, sender, code) need exactly n logged requests, not at least n.

<msg>=seen: a function row of that message's code from its sender on the case's flow, with its objects' group and variation (rules 2, 7 and 9). <msg>=absent: no such row beyond those labelled for other messages. R@<msg>: the outstation's response to that message, judged on the probe log's fc row. W=seen is the route's verdict.

Unless a case's a cell names it: every cause of the closed set is 0 on both ends. Each end's counts are read from that end's own last resync row, and an end that writes no row is judged only by having none; no dnp3_ weird is in weird.log for the flow; no analyzer violation; no budget row; no reporter error; no crash. rows= lists every resync row of the flow, exactly. scanned_octets is judged only where a cell names it. A report case that states its rows in words is judged on those words.
viol=n in a cell counts every analyzer.log row on the case's flow, the PIA's included (D3's M7 on #718; design 3.2 item 16).

A row stamped @<msg> carries the network time of the packet that holds that message's frame (for a multi-frame message, its last frame). @gap is the time Zeek delivers the hole, after the peer's ACK past it and before W. A first row at confirmation is stamped with the confirming fragment's time (design 2.8).

The ctl cell is expected under each of C0, C1p and C2, judged on the rows it names and nothing else. A route case (R1 to R4) is valid only when all three controls show its ctl cell. If any control shows W seen, the case reads unknown for the fix, never pass: it did not reach the failure (HR-23 note 4.2's rule).

Every case whose twins cell names them has these captures too. nofail: the case without X; under all four configurations P, W and Q are seen, and under C2A no resync row. nowrite: the case without W and its response; under all four no code-5 row on the flow, and under C2A the case's counts and rows. otherend: X built from the outstation's side (its addresses, DIR clear, its transport side); under C2A W and Q are seen, and the counts and rows are the case's on o instead of m; under the controls W is absent, except on R4, where W is seen and the outstation's next delivery is lost. Where the failure's content is a request, the other end's twin carries a response of the same kind: throw becomes C0h 81h 00h, 3 application octets, short of the 4-octet response header; overlimit becomes 129, IIN 0 and 3Ch 01h 06h 34,215 times (102,649 application octets); the reads of badchunk, open+badchunk, nofir, firopen and cut become empty responses of the same framing.

The run reports, per route, n of m cases that pass under C2A and are valid under the controls. HR-25 closes only if every case of every route does. A route with a failing or unknown case stays open in HR-25's row or moves to a row of its own (D1's ruling 6879752967 item 5). Routes: R1 a failed frame then a write; R2 a bad header before confirmation then a session; R3 a TCP gap that splits a frame then a write; R4 a link-only frame then a write.

Each TCP gap case opens with the full handshake, the peer's ACK past the hole comes before W, and the case is valid only if conn.log shows missed_bytes on that end and the gap letter for that end in history. Otherwise it reads unknown.
dnp3-resync-udp-r2-idle is valid only if conn.log shows a new uid starting at the bad datagram.
A cell or case marked report is measured and stated, not judged, except that a crash or a reporter error still fails it.
Under C2A no input reaches a reporter error (design 2.9). A reporter error on any input, a case, a twin, the false-positive set, the malformed set or a rerun, fails that input, and is a finding.
The harness reads no payload: not analyzer.log's failure_data, not a weird's addl beyond its name (HR-23 note 4.4). Rows carry causes and counts only.
A case, twin or configuration that did not run is unknown, never pass.
A run counts only from main, with both files at the SHA-256s in pins.env (pin-files) and every capture at the builder's committed hashes (pin-builder). Any other run is a rehearsal.

tests/integration/gt_pcap/resync-cases.tsv and resync-conditions.tsv, pinned by test_resync_conditions.py. D4 adds RESYNC_CASES_SHA256 and RESYNC_CONDITIONS_SHA256, with the values that test holds, to modules/telemetry/experiments/engine-linux/pins.env in deliverable 3. D6 does not edit D4's files.

Owed by D6 under this brief before the counted run, in its own PR: tests/integration/gt_pcap/resync_cases.py writes every case and twin, frame by frame, with dnp3.py; tests/fixtures/network/gt-pcap/resync/ holds their SHA-256s and labels; a6-gt-pcap rebuilds them and checks the hashes and labels. The captures are never committed. Until that PR merges, no run counts.

Requests carry application sequence 0, 1, 2 and on in order, mod 16; each end's transport sequence counts per frame from 0, mod 64. Where a row writes an application control octet as C0h (throw, B400, B401, overlimit, G0, G0r), it stands for FIR and FIN, and its sequence bits take the running value: the octet is C0h | (sequence mod 16). P: read class 0 (g60v1, qualifier 06). W: direct operate, code 5, g12v1 qualifier 28h, index 0, latch on, on-time 1000 ms (dnp3.crob(0)). W5 and Wb: the same at index 5 and 1. W1 and W2: W's fragment in two frames (FIR, then FIN): W1 holds the transport octet and W's application control octet only (14 octets), and W2 W's other 19 application octets (34 octets). W1c, W2c and W3c: W in two or three frames of confirmed user data (link function 3, FCV set). Qa and Qb: Q in two frames. G3a, G3b and G3c: G in three frames. P2 to P5: further class 0 polls. G0r: a read of g0v254 with qualifier 00h, start 0 and stop 0 (C0h 01h 00h FEh 00h 00h 00h), the form SEL-751 Table D.9 lists. W6, W6a and W6b: W as a direct operate without reply (code 6), in two frames split as W1 and W2. Rst: the master's Reset Link States (link function 0, PRM set), 10 octets, which opens every case with confirmed user data; the first confirmed frame then carries FCB 1, each new frame toggles it, and a retry repeats it (inference, IEEE 1815 not held). A: O1's link-layer ACK (link function 0). T: throw. I: an inserted datagram. X, Xm and Xo: the case's failure, from m or o. Rbig: builder-join. B400 and B401: builder-limit. G0: arm-g0. m is the master's end and o the outstation's. Q: read classes 1, 2 and 3 (g60v2, g60v3, g60v4, qualifier 06). R: the outstation's response, code 129, IIN 0, echoing its request's application sequence number, with no objects except R after W, which echoes W's g12v1 (qualifier 28h, index 0) with status 0 (SEL-751 Table D.9: the response to g12v1 is an echo of the request). R(I): R to an inserted I; to I:throw, a malformed read, it carries IIN 0004h, IIN2's parameter error (inference, D2 on #698). G: a second read of Q's content. UDP: M5 192.0.2.14:20000 and O1 192.0.2.20:20000, link 5 and 10. TCP: M1 192.0.2.10, a port from 41100 up, to O1 192.0.2.20:20000, link 1 and 10, with the handshake first and the FIN exchange last unless the build says otherwise. A message of more than one frame (W1 and W2, G3a to G3c, Rbig, B400, B401, overlimit) goes one frame per datagram over UDP and one frame per segment over TCP, unless the build joins frames with +.
A header of link length 0 from M5 (CTRL C4h) whose CRC octets are 05 64, so W's frame starts at its octet 8. Solved over DEST.

The two octets 05 64, immediately before W's frame from M1, so that the false header is 05 64 and W's first 8 octets, and its CRC octets are W's SRC. The test checks that this CRC fails.

garbage(n): n octets with no 05 octet. badhdr: 05 64, six header octets of the sender, a header CRC that fails, and six 00 octets. len(k): a header of link length k with a passing CRC, then six 00 octets. badchunk: P's frame with its chunk CRC's first octet inverted. open+badchunk: frame 1 of a two-frame read (FIR), valid, then frame 2 (FIN) with a bad chunk CRC. nofir: a valid frame with FIN set and FIR clear and 6 octets of object data. firopen: frame 1 of a two-frame read (FIR, no FIN), valid, never followed by its frame 2. throw: a read with one object octet, C0h 01h 3Ch. cut: Q's 24-octet frame cut after 14 octets. holds: a header of link length 53 with a CRC that fails, then three 00 octets, then W's frame (W at offset 13). L, Lm, Lo: link-only frames of 10 octets (L and Lo: link status request, function 9; Lm: link status, function 11). embed(W5): a frame of link length 53 (64 octets) with W5's whole frame at its octets 20 to 54 and 00 elsewhere, which fails its first chunk CRC. embedtail(W5): a frame of link length 53 whose last 4 octets are W5's first 4, its first two chunk CRCs valid and its last failing, followed by W5's other 31 octets. Every generator checks every offset of the failure and the 9 octets after it for a candidate (05 64, a passing header CRC, a length of 5 to 255) other than those the case names, and draws again.

B400: a read of 102,400 application octets: C0h 01h, then 3Ch 01h 06h 34,131 times, then 3Ch 02h 00h 00h 00h. B401: C0h 01h, then 3Ch 01h 06h 34,133 times (102,401). overlimit: C0h 01h, 3Ch 01h 06h 34,214 times and 3Ch 02h 00h 00h 00h (102,649). Frames carry 249 application octets each, except that overlimit's first 412 frames sum to exactly 102,400 and its last holds 249, and B400's and B401's last frames hold the remainder. One frame per datagram (builder-msgs), so about 412 datagrams each; the transport sequence wraps mod 64.

Rbig: O1's response of 2,048 application octets (129, IIN 0, g1v2 qualifier 01h indices 0 to 2036, flags 01h), in 9 frames: 8 of 292 octets and 1 of 75. The capture starts at its frame 2, so the sensor sees 8 frames of 2,119 octets, none with FIR, one frame per datagram or segment, with transport sequence 1 to 8.

P4-4-HR2325S deliverable 3 (design 3.2). A token without a number takes its end's next transport number when built (builder-msgs); m numbered from n sets m's next to n. W1, W2 and W3 in one cell: W in three frames of unconfirmed user data, split as W1c to W3c are. seg(n): a frame from the sender, FIR and FIN clear, number n, and one application octet, 22h, function code 34 in the fragment it joins (arm-3bdata); seg(n,ctl=T) carries frame T's control octet, and seg(n,dest=11) goes to link 11, not O1's 10. sub(n,dest=11): as seg, built to take the place of a frame of W that the capture leaves out, so the fragment it joins is whole and in sequence. firopen(n): firopen numbered n. fin(T), octet(T), fewer(T), more(T), same(T), fcb(T): frame T as built, with its transport FIN set; its first application octet inverted; without its last application octet; with 00h added at its end; unchanged; its FCB toggled; each with T's control octet and addresses. read(T): T's control and transport octets, to link 11, with application octets 01h 3Ch 01h 06h, so that after W1c's application control octet it is a read of g60v1 (D6's R2 on #782). badobj: a 129 of 5 application octets, IIN 0000h and one object octet, 3Ch, which the response parser rejects (HR-23 design 4.7). fc(c,n): one frame of n application octets, C0h with the sequence, code c, then 00h; fc2(c,n): the same in two frames, the first with 2. lostmiddle: o's empty response in three frames, split as W1c to W3c, its frame 2 left out of the capture. embedhead: a frame of link length 53 whose CTRL and DEST octets are 05 64, so that a candidate starts at its offset 3, whose DEST high and SRC low are the frame's header CRC; its first chunk CRC fails, and its other chunks are 00h with valid CRCs. embedlast(W5): as embedtail, with W5's first octet as the frame's last octet, in its third chunk CRC, which fails, and W5's other 34 octets after it. overlimit[first] and overlimit[rest]: overlimit's frame 1, and its frames 2 to 413. R(T): the response to message T, sent whether or not T was whole on the wire. no handshake: a TCP cell that starts without the handshake. Labels read a fragment by rule (A), C2A's parser choice: fc is labelled absent only where it throws by that rule (an object arm with 1 or 2 object octets), and a retry after a primary link-only frame of its end is no link-layer retry (design 2.3).

D2's unknown object is g0v254, qualifier 06h, in a read (G0: C0h 01h 00h FEh 06h). dnp3-protocol.pac at v9.0.1 (SHA-256 497eeac4...) takes default -> objects: empty in Request_Objects for an object_type_field it does not list, and Object_Header reads no range for qualifier 6. A read's object carries no data, so nothing is left to misread, and G0 parses. G0r, with qualifier 00h, reads Range_Field_0 (start_index and stop_index, one octet each; number_of_item 1) and then takes the same default arm, so it parses too. g60 is not listed either, so P takes the same arm (D4 on #698, 6894466378). Desk; that a Request_Objects array ends at the end of its record is generated code, not read. The four unknown-object cases pin that branch: if G0 or G0r throws, they fail, and the reading is wrong.

From dnp3-protocol.pac at v9.0.1: DNP3_Request's empty arms are codes 0, 13, 14, 15, 19, 23 and 24, and its default arm, bytestring &restofdata, takes codes 34 to 255, of which (i) sends 129 to 131 to the response parser. A (3b-data) item labelled to parse uses an empty-arm code with 2 application octets, or a code from 34 to 128 or 132 to 255 with 2 or more. A (3c) item uses a code whose arm parses objects (1 to 12, 16 to 18, 20 to 22, 25 to 33) with exactly 1 object octet. No item uses a code with an object arm and no object octet, whose result rests on generated code that was not read.

HR-23 note 4.3's UDP classes, each item on its own 5-tuple, run under all four configurations, plus class (6) over TCP. Where HR-23's stage-2 pins set a larger floor for the same class, the larger holds for both runs.

The generators of classes (1), (2), (3a), (4), (5) and (6) compute the header CRC at every offset where 05 64 occurs (for (6), in each end's stream) and draw again when one passes (T7, D6's B1). Classes (1), (2), (4) and (5) then hold no frame whose header and every chunk CRC pass, and carry no gap, so under the five-cause rule they write no row.
05 64 and 0 to 8 more octets, at least 33 items of each length.
A header CRC that fails, in a datagram of 11 to 1,472 octets.
DNS, NetBIOS name service and LLMNR queries with ID 0564h, and RADIUS Accounting-Responses (code 5, identifier 64h), at least 75 of each protocol.
Random payloads forced to start 05 64, NTP, Syslog and SNMP among them.
Under C2A, per class, both readings (conn.log's service, and a link row).
Under C2A, per class: no end row, no budget row, no dnp3_ weird. Zero in 300 bounds the rate per flow at about 1% at 95% (rule of three), per class.
Size. Under C2A: never named under conn.log's reading (C0 names it), the link-row reading unknown; chunk_crc counted; no end row, since chunk_crc is not one of the five causes.

Size, with every empty-arm code at least twice and at least 16 items from the default arm. Under C2A each is named at its first fragment, as under C0 (a false positive recorded under HR-23 (3c) and R-1, not closed), and its later datagram without the magic writes a first row with magic=1.
Size. Under C2A: never named, no resync row.
Size. Under C2A: never named, no violation, app_parse=1 and one end row on the sender's end per item.
Non-DNP3 TCP flows on tcp/20000 with the full handshake: HTTP/1.1 text, TLS-shaped records, an SSH banner then random octets, random octets; 50 to 5,000 octets per end, so that some reach O.
The same, each with one acknowledged hole under judge-r3.

Named under C2A. Their end rows are exactly one per flow with a hole, on the end with it, with gap=1. Their budget rows are exactly the flows that the generator labels as reaching O or F before the end, by construction. No other resync row.

Per class, under each configuration: the flows named under each reading, the end rows, the budget rows, and the gap rows on unnamed flows (6893732701), each with the class's size. Never netted out against a control. C1p, which writes no resync row, is the control for the three row counts; C0's named count is reported beside.

column2: HR-23 note 4.3's malformed set, under C2A
column5: Each input on its own 5-tuple, judged under C2A against this row and not against C2: 1 to 3 octets: truncated; lengths 0 to 4 with a passing CRC: link_length, a failed header, and no AddToBuffer reporter error; a length of 5 with trailing bytes: the trailing bytes are read from the header stage; a datagram longer than its frame: its tail counted as truncated or scanned; two frames in one datagram: both parsed; a frame of length 255: parsed, no AnalyzerError; a fragment without FIR: first_chunk_missing; without FIN then a new FIR: fir_restart; beyond the limit: fragment_limit; 1 application octet, and a code of 129 to 131 with 2 or 3 octets, from either side: app_parse; class (2): no violation before confirmation. Each failure is counted and parsing goes on. A length of 6 (a transport octet and no application octet) passes on either branch: app_parse=1, or no count, with no crash and no reporter error.

column2: the four TCP inputs held at the connection's end, under C2A
column5: A good header then a bad chunk CRC then a TCP FIN: chunk_crc=1 and nothing held at the FIN, so no app_parse. A link length of 4 with FIR and no DNP3 FIN then a TCP FIN: link_length=1 and nothing held. A fragment with FIR and no DNP3 FIN then a TCP FIN, and the same left open to the capture's end: either branch passes, app_parse=1 on that end or no count, with no crash, no reporter error and no violation; FlowEOF runs on that end's own interpreter inside A's catch.
Rows of engine-pass-conditions.tsv, at its pin, that C2 passes and C2A fails. No E-D4-03 row regresses (the brief's acceptance test).
Every GT-PCAP DNP3 case, every HR-23 stage-2 case, the PRP pairs, the public captures and E2's corpus rows run under C2 and C2A.

Per flow, C2A against C2: the Protocol, Service, Function, Objects and group 120 verdicts; the probe's link rows (uid, is_orig, server) and fc rows (uid, is_orig, code, objects). Allowed to differ: a link row's time where its frame spans segments, the time of confirmation, and resync rows and resync_cause on a flow where C2A counts a cause. Any other difference is a regression of A, and fails.

No GT-PCAP DNP3 case starts inside a flow (engine-pass-conditions.tsv has no midstream DNP3 row). HR-23's dnp3-udp-relay-write, dnp3-udp-relay-restart and dnp3-tcp-master-short start mid-session at a whole fragment, so their rows are expected equal under C2A, with the time of confirmation allowed to differ.

Under C2A against C2, the engine's output gains exactly: the events dnp3_resync and dnp3_resync_mark; the weirds dnp3_invalid_link_length, dnp3_embedded_header, dnp3_fragment_restarted, dnp3_app_parse_failed, dnp3_content_gap, dnp3_truncated_frame, dnp3_resync_budget_exhausted and dnp3_invariant; otsec_probe.log rows of kind resync with the fields why, cause, counts, scanned_octets and overflow; and the field resync_cause on fc rows. Anything else new fails.

Rows are counted against K on a grid of network time anchored at the script's first resync row. Every resync row but the overflow row counts, whatever its why. An overflow row is written for an interval only if a row was held back in it, by a timer at the interval's end or at zeek_done for the last one. dnp3-resync-udp-report-cap pins it.

Reporter.cc at v9.0.1 (SHA-256 9bdb6c05...), PermitNetWeird: a weird on Weird::sampling_global_list is allowed while its host-wide count is at most sampling_threshold (25), then when (count - 25) is a multiple of sampling_rate (1000); the count resets sampling_duration (10 min) after its first. So n weirds of one name within 10 min raise 25 + floor((n - 25) / 1000) events, for n above 25.

weird.zeek at v9.0.1 (SHA-256 a8b6e525...), do_weird: the default action is ACTION_LOG, and after a row is logged the pair (name, connection) is ignored for 10 min (weird_ignore). So weird.log shows at most one row of a name per connection per 10 min, and the host-wide bound shows only across connections. The weird counts in resync-cases.tsv are weird.log rows.

Judged on the coverage replay of the final (i)+A corpus of each target, inside the job (design 5). Reached means a hit count of 1 or more on the site's line, or on each named arm of its branch; not reached means 0. D4 commits, with A's patch, a site map naming each cov- site below by file, function and line at the patch's SHA-256; D6 reviews it before the run. Without it, the condition is unknown.

Reached: the branch that counts each of magic, header_crc, link_length, chunk_crc, embedded_header, first_chunk_missing, fir_restart, app_parse and budget (budget is reachable at val-F and val-O within fuzz-max-len).

Reached: the drop function, and both arms of its branch on a fragment in progress: remake (cov-drop-remake) and keep (cov-drop-keep). That an idle end keeps its interpreter cannot be seen in a capture run (D6's N6), so these arms are its evidence.

Reached: the remake arm on an end whose interpreter holds an incomplete unit, followed in the same input by a parse on that end. Shown by the converted seeds dnp3-resync-*-chunk-crc-open and dnp3-resync-*-fir-restart, which do exactly that, replayed under ASan with no report.
Reached: the 10-octet link-only path; the link length 0 to 4 path; the embedded-header check, both its found and its not-found arms; the catch inside ProcessData's loop.
Reached: truncated's branch; the reset at a datagram's end with a fragment open; the scan inside a datagram.
Reached: gap's branch, from Undelivered; the scan holding a partial candidate across chunks; the embedded check holding octets across chunks.

Not reached: each of AddToBuffer's three guards, ParseAppLayer's overflow guard, ProcessData's pkt_length <= 0 check, invariant's branch, and the catches in DNP3_TCP_Analyzer::DeliverStream and DNP3_UDP_Analyzer::DeliverPacket. A reach is a finding, and fails the run.
fragment_limit, which val-limit puts out of reach of fuzz-max-len. Stated in the result, never counted as reached.
At least O plus a session (val-O). A seed that does not fit in 4,096 octets and 64 chunks is listed as not converted, never cut.
Seconds per input. A loop that makes no progress (design 2.1) shows as a timeout, which is a report.
libFuzzer's default, stated so that it is pinned.
On (detect_leaks=1), so that an interpreter not freed on remake is a report.
The same for every campaign.
After each mutation the custom mutator leaves each header CRC and each chunk CRC as mutated with this probability, drawn from its Seed argument, and recomputes the rest.
Seconds per target per build: 2 targets x 3 builds. If cov- is not met at the end, the result is unknown, and D1 rules a longer run; the run is never repeated with new seeds until it passes.

Before the campaigns, the job checks that no seed from Zeek's dnp3_tcp corpus, the malformed set or the HR-23 cases sets bit 7 (80h) of a FuzzBuffer flag byte, and that in each converted dnp3-resync-* case bit 7 is set exactly on the chunks the case labels as holes. Either check failing stops the job.
Zeek's dnp3_tcp corpus, the malformed set, the HR-23 cases, and every dnp3-resync-* case and twin that fits fuzz-max-len, converted by the pinned script. The job lists those not converted.

User plus system CPU time of the zeek -r process, minus that of a run on a capture that holds only its file header, as the median of s5-runs runs, on the counted run's runner image, with the shipped script loaded (D3's N1). A run without that script does not count.
The median of 7 runs, each on a fresh process.
Of DNP3 link-layer octets, within one frame, for each input and for each transport's valid baseline.

Each against valid DNP3 of the same transport and size (P R W R Q R repeated): (1) the smallest throwing fragment, throw, packed into 1,472-octet datagrams or a TCP stream after one P R; (2) pairs of a 13-octet FIR-only frame and a 13-octet frame with a bad chunk CRC, a remake without an exception; (3) 13-octet frames without FIR after confirmation; (4) the same on a connection that never confirms (D6's B7); (5) 05 64 repeated; (6) builder-c1-udp-4 repeated, a chain in which every header's CRC octets start the next; (7) after one P R, builder-s5-7's frames back to back, five to a 1,472-octet datagram or in a TCP stream, which drive the embedded-header check at its densest with a candidate in every frame (D3's N1 on #698). Each input is valid only if its counts match how it was built: app_parse equal to its fragments; chunk_crc equal to its pairs; first_chunk_missing equal to its frames, with no budget row; no candidate in (5); link_length equal to its datagrams in (6); chunk_crc and embedded_header each equal to its frames in (7).

The last 10 octets of every frame of input (7): 05 64 05 64 05 64 05 64 and its header CRC, 82 E4 (E482h). Each frame is m's header of link length 255 (292 octets), then 05 64 repeated over its offsets 10 to 281, then these 10 octets at 282 to 291. Every chunk CRC fails. The check finds 05 64 at every even offset from 10 to 288, so it computes 140 header CRCs per frame, one fewer than with 05 64 alone, which gives no candidate because 82 E4 is not 05 64 (D3's N1 on #698). Offset 282 is the one candidate, a header of link length 5, whether a datagram's end or the next frame follows; it is the last offset at which a whole candidate fits inside the frame, so a check that stops at its first candidate still computes every header CRC before it. The test checks each of these facts.
Each input's median, the baseline's, and their ratio, per transport, judged against val-ratio. The measurement comes before the image the counted run measures is fixed (design 2.10).
